review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: REST/API homonym repair; HTTP protocol, messages and method semantics; URI/URL distinctions; network API intersections and software client/server roles in U3.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet; CC BY 4.0 and Princeton notices remain in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. IETF specifications, Fielding and MDN support technical corrections and extensions. No source definitions, algorithms or code are copied. Labels, scope restrictions and graph mappings are editorial adaptations.
review.context_policy: All new concepts and new assertions use the IT universe U3, with unspecified strength. The one rejected rest/API assertion remains as U1 history. Existing home contexts and prior U1/U3 assertions remain unchanged. No automatic projection of the new technical taxonomy into U1.

sense_decisions.scope: A set of architectural design constraints for software systems.
Representational State Transfer as a complete architectural style.
An API accessible over a network, without requiring HTTP.
A network API using HTTP, without implying REST conformance.
An API whose interaction design follows the REST constraints.
The intersection of HTTP use and REST-conforming design.
The HTTP protocol family, without a TCP-only or browser-only restriction.
The information carried as an HTTP request or response.
An HTTP request message.
An HTTP response message.
The named request semantics, distinct from an execution event.
Repetition has the same intended effect; responses may differ.
Read-only requested semantics; this is not a security guarantee.
The standard GET method for retrieving a representation.
The standard HEAD method with no response content.
The standard POST method for resource-specific processing.
The standard PUT method with replacement semantics.
The standard DELETE method; no guarantee of physical data erasure.
An information object identifying a resource. A programming-language name is a separate selected sense.
A resource identifier using URI syntax; identification need not supply a location.
The locator subset of URIs under RFC 3986. Correct the dictionary restriction to web pages.
A URL whose scheme is http.
A URL whose scheme is https.
A code describing the result represented by an HTTP response.
Processing an HTTP request.
Sending an HTTP request.
Software acting in the HTTP server role.
Software acting in the HTTP client role.
An HTTP request whose method is GET.
An HTTP request whose method is HEAD.
Do not place resource identifiers beneath the existing programming-language construct merely because both use the word identifier.
An architecture and a style constraining architectures are not automatically the same kind of information object; retain the existing architecture branch.
The existing server has a hardware genus and a Jenkins child; its broader hardware/software ambiguity needs a separate reviewed split.
The existing client is hardware. New HTTP client software is explicitly qualified rather than silently changing the old genus.
Protocol links to social communication and generic standard remain queued; not every proprietary communication protocol is a public standard.
Preserve rest, its physiological genus, its child and all unrelated facts. Only the mistaken API attribute is rejected.
The dictionary architectural-style synset concerns an art form, not software constraints.

review.limits: REST means the full architectural style, not any JSON or HTTP interface. Safe methods concern requested semantics, not security or absence of logging. Idempotence does not require identical responses. URI and URL use RFC 3986 scope; not every URL addresses a web page. No protocol implementation, networking request, performance guarantee, caching rule, transport-only restriction or automatic retry instruction is added. Existing hardware server/client, programming-identifier, architecture and protocol/standard distinctions remain queued for wider review. No application test suites.

exclusion_review.decision: Preserve all exclusions and explicit negations. Check the IT context separately because the new taxonomy is U3-only. No new pair or witness is accepted.

review.collision_decision: No exact normalized cross-language collision is accepted. Qualified REST and software-role terms avoid the existing rest and hardware senses. The ambiguous bare REST acronym is not added as a new alias. Existing API, protocol, request, response and processing/sending actions are reused.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Normalized spelling candidates are not verified identities or missing-concept counts.
